title: Interactive RAG playground: embedded scenario simulator + browser instrumentation
author: Asha Menon
description:
Summary: Adds a new interactive RAG playground quickstart that runs an embedded scenario simulator in the browser using WASM for deterministic tool stubs, plus lightweight instrumentation hooks for tracing token-level events and exporter snippets for the Redwood Console. Motivation: teams often need a fast, local-first way to prototype multi-tool RAG flows and reproduce user-session behaviors without standing up backend services. This quickstart provides a single-page dev experience that can run offline, replay recorded traces, and emit a minimal event stream compatible with Redwood Console's local debug mode.

What this PR contains (single-string sectioned description):
- Quickstart scaffold: a self-contained SPA (HTML+TS) under quickstarts/playground-sim that loads a pre-bundled WASM stub runtime and a tiny in-memory vector store. The page exposes a stepper UI to drive scenarios, capture prompts, and snapshot KV cache states.
- WASM tool stubs: wasm/tool-stub.wasm + TypeScript bindings. The stubs emulate external tool calls (search, code-exec, HTTP fetch) deterministically so replayed scenarios are identical across machines.
- Instrumentation SDK: quickstarts/playground-sim/instrumentation.ts introduces a small event API (emitEvent/flush) and an exporter shim that can push events to Redwood Console's local ingest endpoint or persist to localStorage for offline replay.
- Docs: docs/quickstarts/playground-sim.md with a step-by-step tutorial, screenshots, and a troubleshooting section. Also adds a short note to docs/CONTRIBUTING.md about including reproducible scenario data when opening quickstart PRs.
- Tests & CI: a tiny Jest scenario runner and snapshot tests (tests/scenario-runner.test.ts) to ensure WASM stubs produce stable outputs. CI updates add a job to build WASM with wasm-pack and run the scenario snapshots on Linux.

How to try locally:
1) git checkout feature/rag-playground-sim-embed
2) cd quickstarts/playground-sim && npm ci && npm run start
3) Open http://localhost:3000, select a scenario from the left panel and press Play.
4) To replay stored traces, open the Replay tab and select saved snapshots.
5) To push events to Redwood Console's local debug ingest, set REW_CONSOLE_URL in the UI to your local console address.

Motivation and design notes: The simulator emphasizes determinism: WASM stubs return stable outputs for a given input seed so snapshot tests and cross-machine debugging match. Instrumentation exposes token-level boundaries where possible without adding large dependencies; the exporter is intentionally pluggable so teams can wire to their own observability pipeline. The quickstart is intentionally small — it's a developer toy for prototyping orchestration and tool-calling flows before migrating to production Redwood runtimes.

Testing performed: unit snapshot tests for two canonical scenarios (faq-assistant, code-retri eval); manual browser runs on macOS and Linux; CI runs wasm-pack build and node-based snapshot runner.

Migration and rollout: docs/quickstarts/index.md updated to link this new entry. No migrations required for production code.

Related: Linear ENG-1453 (quickstarts: interactive RAG playground), PM-92 (product validation).

Release notes: Adds an interactive RAG playground quickstart (WASM-based tool stubs, instrumentation hooks, and scenario snapshot tests). This is a developer QA/demo utility only and is not intended for production traffic.
